Fixes #19114

## Summary
The bug is due to the fact that to read the hooks the debug tools use the real object ref. The problem is that if this object is modified by the debug tools it is never cleaned (in our case we created a new function with a dummy setstate). So my fix is to make a shallow copy for the useref case. Maybe we have to do it for all hooks or do a deep copy?

> The problem is that if this object is modified by the debug tools it is never cleaned

The debug tools don't modify the object, right? That's being done by app code with side effects?

> The debug tools don't modify the object, right? That's being done by app code with side effects?

Sorry I'm not very clear.  
What's happening:

1.  When we render App it creates an object1
2.  The button onClick handler use object1 
3.  The debug tools render App  and use object1
4. object1.current is modified with a dummy setstate
5. The button onClick handler use always object1

I'm not sure if I'm clear.

Right. It was "the debug tools" comment that confused me, since the debug tools (`ReactDebugHooks`) don't modify anything. It's application code in this case that's modifying the ref during render (which isn't a safe or supported pattern.)
Tagging @gaearon and @sebmarkbage  for a second opinion about the added warning.

I like the idea and agree that dev/prod should match.

I'm not sure if the added prod overhead is worth the error so I defer to others to make the call.

> I'm not sure if the added prod overhead is worth the error so I defer to others to make the call.

If it helps, just to clarify, this change is being made to the `react-debug-tools` package (so DevTools, not React itself).
Oh right, I missed that. I'm +1 then!

Mixed feelings about this conclusion.

I agree that the underlying problem of mutations during renders needs to be addressed, and a halfway warning fix is not great. (I'd like to see us add warnings in DEV for primitive ref hook too FWIW.)

Status quo at the moment is pretty rough though. React does some atypical stuff and components end up subtly broken in some cases. Discoverability is low.
Let's close this in favor of a more comprehensive approach via #18545 ?

issue_context.title: Bug: React Devtools incorrectly updates the setter function of useState hooks
issue_context.body:
From the docs: > React guarantees that setState function identity is stable and won’t change on re-renders. This is why it’s safe to omit from the useEffect or useCallback dependency list. When React Devtools is opened, new `setState` is created on each rendering, which could lead to inconsistencies. React version: 16.13.1 ## Steps To Reproduce 1. Open the [codesandbox](https://codesandbox.io/s/react-devtools-suspense-bug-hqwuq?file=/src/App.js). 2. Click the "Open in new window" button beside the codesandbox browser url. 3. On the new page which is running the code, open the React Devtools `Component` tab. 4. Click on the `App` Component. 5. Refresh the page and click the button "Component updates xx times". 6. Nothing is updated. 7. Close devtools, refresh, click the button again, update works fine. ```jsx // This component is created solely for // pointing out the bug function App() { const updateCountRef = useRef(0) updateCountRef.current++ const [state, setState] = useState('A'); const cbRef = useRef() cbRef.current = () => { setState(c => String.fromCharCode(c.charCodeAt(0) + 1)) } const handler = () => cbRef.current() return (

Current state value: {state}

) } ``` Link to code example: ## The current behavior - Component does not update when React Devtools is opened. - New `setState` is created on each rendering. ## The expected behavior - Component should update on each click. - There should be only one `setState`.
comments:
>AFAIK it's just a variable assignment to the ref.

It's a mutation in render, which makes it impure. That can cause issues if a render doesn't end up getting committed to the screen. (However, in this particular case it doesn't seem like it would matter since you're not using any props/state in the closure.)
Oh! I see it now. I'll try updating the callbacks after render phase and see if it works. Thanks for the hints.
I don't actually understand why the state update is ignored though. I'm confused by this.

One more question regarding concurrent mode. Is it safe/recommended to use layout effects for this purpose?

```js
useIsomorphicLayoutEffect(() => {
  argsRef.current = args
})
```

Adding this works with React Devtools and passes all my current tests. I am also using the `Scheduler` mock for [testing tearing](https://github.com/crimx/observable-hooks/blob/3933a21f048b164a9bca6b24315d53affaaa7f48/packages/observable-hooks/__tests__/concurrent-mode.spec.tsx#L30-L107). How can I stop a render being committed? So that I can test correctness of the callbacks in ref.
I mean since the layout effects run synchronously, with the Scheduler mock I am not able to find a way to break the jobs right before them.

review_comments: This is a stand-in for a more helpful warning, should we agree that this change is worth adding.
I think warning about this type of (bad) mutation would be a useful addition. Cloning in prod is also necessary to make DEV and prod behavior match.
